tofa for Kodi Design Language

Every distinctly-styled control in the add-on's window UI — cards, pills, rows, badges, input, panels — in every state it actually renders, with the exact fill/border/radius/font/color values behind it. Built from fragments.py, theme.py, fontinstall.py and the hand-authored screen XML, not eyeballed off screenshots.

Real typefaces (Inter Tight, Roboto Mono) and the real Lucide icon glyphs are embedded — this renders in the exact fonts the live app uses. See the icon reference tool for the full 2,027-icon Lucide catalog; this page only shows the glyphs already wired into a component.

Foundations

tofa's internal TV-DESIGN.md spec defines these as cross-platform tokens (Android TV + tvOS); values below are what's actually implemented in this Kodi client, called out where it drifts from spec.

Surface ladder

Accent (runtime variable, 14 presets)

windows/theme.py:PRESETS

Sourced from the signed-in account's own server-side preference (/api/v1/users/me), never a hardcoded hex — the local Kodi setting is only an offline fallback. One accent at a time everywhere: pill fills, focus borders, progress bars, the fox logo (which snaps to whichever of these 14 raster variants is nearest by RGB distance — it can't be tinted arbitrarily like flat chrome can).

Text tiers (white-alpha)

theme.py:TEXT_PRIMARY/TEXT_STRONG/TEXT_SECONDARY/TEXT_TERTIARY

RESOLVED (2026-07-30), then reopened by measurement (2026-08-13): there are FOUR tiers, not three. Spec §2 defines four of its own (100/62/42/24%); the codebase had drifted to ~18 distinct alpha values for text. The 2026-07-30 pass consolidated that to three, each confirmed by pixel-sampling real Apple TV reference captures rather than copied from the spec sight-unseen — alpha = (rendered−background)/(255−background) against the measured local background — and it explicitly found the 80–82% band empty in both the captures and the codebase, which is why three was the answer and not four. Spec's own fourth tier ("muted", 24%) had no callers and still has none.

What reopened it: §8.8's pause card. Its "N min left" line measures a peak of 211 against its own clock's 251 on the live Apple TV — ~83%, landing squarely in that supposedly-empty band. Under "the shipped app is the design source" a measured value outranks the tidiness of a three-bucket split, so TEXT_STRONG (0xD4, 83%) exists. It has exactly one user, and theme.py's own comment says to keep it that way until another label is measured into it: a tier that starts collecting labels by eye is how the ~18 values this system replaced got here in the first place. Treat it as a measured exception, not as a general-purpose "slightly brighter than secondary".

Every tier is pushed as a Window.Property (text_primary/text_strong/text_secondary/text_tertiary) in each window's onFirstInit, and <textcolor> references the property rather than the hex — 182 primary, 104 secondary, 48 tertiary, 1 strong across the generated pipeline and the hand-authored screens. The 2026-07-30 claim that zero literal white-alpha textcolors remain is no longer true; three have reappeared since, see Findings.

primarywhite · ~97%
strongD4 · 83%
secondary9E · 62%
tertiary6B · 42%

Typography — tofa_font_* roles

resources/lib/fontinstall.py:FONTS

Inter Tight carries every text role, in three weights — and weight is a property of the file, not a tag: Kodi's <font> has no weight attribute, so "SemiBold" means fontinstall.py injected inter_tight_semibold.ttf under that role name. Three roles are Roboto Mono, and only three: sign-in's tofa_font_link and tofa_font_code (a pairing code has to survive being read aloud off a TV), and tofa_font_stats_value in the player's §8.11 stats readout, where the numbers tick once a second and a proportional face would shuffle the whole row sideways every time a digit changed width. Ratings and PIN digits are not mono — the rating badge is tofa_font_micro and the PIN pad is tofa_font_button. The eight Lucide roles at the bottom are one per pixel footprint the UI actually draws at.

Sizes are not one conversion. The page used to say every size here was ~1.75× a spec point size; that is true of one group only, and stating it as a blanket rule invites the wrong arithmetic on the rest. There are three conventions in play, and which one a role used is recorded beside it in fontinstall.py:

  • §3's type scale, ×1.7 from half-density. The spec's own preamble says its Android TV numbers are dp at half density and that absolute sizes scale to the platform canvas. Six roles came straight through it: hero 44→77, screen title 32→57, section title 22→39, row title 15→26, body 14→24, metadata 13→23.
  • 1:1, where the spec section is already on our canvas. §7.2 is 1:1 (its row label of 26 is tofa_font_row_title), so its "34/Bold" panel title is a literal 34 — tofa_font_dialog_title. Multiplying it would have been the mistake.
  • Cap-height conversion, measured off the real Apple TV. The newest roles were sized by measuring the app's own ink and converting through Inter Tight's metrics rather than reusing a nominal point size across two different typefaces. Inter Tight's cap is 0.7275/em, Roboto Mono's ~0.71, so §7.3's "50pt bold" Top Result title becomes 52, not 50 and not 87: 50pt of SF Pro caps at 38px, and 52 of Inter Tight is what reproduces 38. The player title (cap 34→45), subtitle (22→30), pause clock (37→51), and all four §8.11 stats roles came the same way. Two of them also corrected a weight the same way: the pause clock reads regular, not the bold heading role it used to borrow (stroke-to-height 0.108/0.135, which bold overshoots at 0.216), and the line under it reads bold, not the semibold button role it used to borrow.

§3's own mapping is not exempt either. The hero was 77 by that ×1.7 rule and had never been measured, because the app draws the title's LOGO there and only falls back to text when a title has none — a case no stored capture contained. Captured live on 2026-08-19 and it read 30% over: the Home fallback caps at 43px (Inter Tight 59), Detail's at 46px (63). What makes it interesting is that the SAME 77 measured exactly right on the server picker, whose heading caps at 56px — so the number was never wrong, it was wrong for two of its three callers. It now splits: tofa_font_hero keeps 77 and heads a screen, tofa_font_hero_title is 61 and stands in for artwork.

So: sizes below are Kodi's actual injected values, read out of FONTS at generation time. Don't back-derive a spec number from one by dividing — and don't assume a role that was derived rather than measured is right just because it has shipped for months.

Corner radius

border="N" 9-patch crops + exact-size mask assets

Kodi's <texture border="N"> is a literal N×N pixel crop of the source PNG's own baked corner — not a resolution-independent radius — so every distinct radius below is a distinct source asset, not one parameter. Spec §4 calls for a 4-step scale (8 / 12 / 14 / pill); the codebase had drifted to 9 numbers in use, but a 2026-07-30 pass (see Findings) found several of those were the same ~4px asset wearing different border= labels — the genuinely distinct radii below are down to 7.

Cards

Every card in the app shares one construction: mask/border/glow drawn as exact-size assets (not stretched 9-patch) so the corner radius never warps under focus-zoom.

Pills & Buttons

Everything clickable that isn't a full list row reduces to a filled or outlined rounded rect, optionally with a leading icon and/or trailing chevron.

Rows & Lists

Sidebar rows, history rows, and picker rows all share the same accent-left-bar-on-active convention, each re-implemented by hand once per screen.

Badges & Indicators

Small, non-interactive (or barely-interactive) overlays: ratings, watchlist state, format tags, watched/lock markers.

Input Controls

Keyboard tiles, numeric keypad keys, and device-code tiles — all a square/circular key with a resting-vs-focused fill swap.

Panels, Facts & Empty States

Dialog chrome and the two recurring "nothing here" layouts.

Player Chrome

Transport bar and buffering overlay — the one surface that isn't part of the fragments.py pipeline at all, still fully hand-authored XML.

Consolidation findings

What building this catalog actually surfaced — concrete candidates for the "more template elements, fewer varieties" half of the brief, not just documentation.
